name: MetalBase
tagline: Early-1990s freeware relational DBMS in C with curses data entry and a report writer; archive only.
description: MetalBase was a small relational database package written in C by Richard P. Jernigan IV and shared over FTP and Usenet in the early 1990s. Version 5.0 (1992) bundled a C library with AVL-tree indexes and file locking, a curses-based data-entry interface, a template-driven report writer, field encryption and a converter for older 4.x relation files, and it built on Unix as well as MS-DOS. Development stopped in the mid-1990s; the only known copy of the source is a 2018 archive mirror created while researching dbdb.io, and its original license terms are unknown. It is a museum piece showing how hobbyist databases were built before MySQL and SQLite.
statusNote: Abandoned in the mid-1990s; only an archived source mirror (apavlo/metalbase) remains.

pricing.notes: Distributed free of charge; source available only from an archive mirror.

strengths: Compact, readable C codebase from the pre-SQLite era
Shows a complete small RDBMS toolkit: library, data entry UI and report writer
weaknesses: Abandoned for three decades with unclear licensing
No SQL, no transactions and only basic locking
useCases: Reading a small AVL-tree index implementation
